citations.F1: Replace the per-event actor `fetchrow` with one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` batch fetch (or a join) — 1,912 events currently mean 1,913 round trips
citations.F3: Make `lookup_geo` non-blocking — it uses `requests` inside an async handler, so each uncached IP freezes the whole worker's event loop for up to 2 s
citations.F4: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)` — no index starts with `org_id`
citations.F5: Bound `_request_timings` — it grows one float per request forever at ~120 req/s ... swap it for a fixed-size deque or a counter/bucket histogram
citations.F6: Bound `_geo_cache` too — it is keyed on client IP and never evicted ... use an LRU with a max size and a TTL.
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal — 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections ... a Redis cache is optional after this
citations.F11: would want a shorter key set than `(org_id, since, limit)`, since `since` defaults to a per-request timestamp and never repeats
